pr_title: Split IHttpHeadersHandler into internal and pubinternal copies

issue_context.title: Separate IHttpHeadersHandler public API from internal one
issue_context.body:
`IHttpHeadersHandler` is a pubinternal API. i.e. public API in an internal namespace. It is here because IHttpParser uses it which is also pubinternal. HttpParser is used by platform benchmarks in TechEmpower.

`IHttpHeadersHandler` is also shared code between dotnet/runtime and dotnet/aspnetcore. It used for HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 header parsing. Because it is shared, and because it is pubinternal, there are a bunch of #ifdefs.

https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/774554dfeddd3450f31d979c56060b0451dd49d7/src/Shared/runtime/IHttpHeadersHandler.cs#L5-L18

I think we should just have two copies of `IHttpHeadersHandler` in our code. There appears to be a line between what is used in HTTP/1.1 (pubinternal type) and HTTP/2 & 3 (internal type)
* Pubinternal `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.Kestrel.Core.Internal.Http.IHttpHeadersHandler`. Used by `IHttpParser` and HTTP/1.1.
* Internal `System.Net.Http.IHttpHeadersHandler`. From shared code. Used by HTTP/2 and HTTP/3.

Now we can easily add new methods to the internal interface. The only downside is having to disambiguate the two types in some files.

Thoughts?

Update: Will rename the internal type to `IHttpStreamHeadersHandler` to avoid conflicts.

review_comments: These probably don't need to be on the public interface. You only put them here to minimize breaks, right?

While true, it looks like we've already shipped it starting in .NET 5. I don't see a reason to take another breaking change right now. If we do decide to break it and keep only what we need, we should probably send it through API review and do it all at once. We don't need the `bool endStream` for HTTP/1.x either for example.
Yeah, I left it unchanged to avoid breaks.
